chunks: Fadala ibn Sinan narrated from Sayf, from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ, from Jābir, from al-Waṣṣāfī, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:
Charity given secretly extinguishes the Lord’s wrath, and being kind to parents and keeping ties with near relatives increases lifespans.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of secret charity and maintaining family ties according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the spiritual purification of secret charity (sadaqat al-sirr) with the social obligations of filial piety (birr al-walidayn) and kinship ties (silat al-rahim). In Shia tradition, these acts are not only moral imperatives but also metaphysical causes for extending one's lifespan (mudda) and appeasing divine wrath, reflecting the interconnectedness of individual worship and communal harmony.
